title: Chapter 88 — Campaigns, Events, and The Retail Calendar
intro: The promo calendar mastered, the event playbook, and staying productive during quiet seasons.

sections.title: The Retail Calendar Is Predictable
sections.content:
Appliance retail follows a predictable annual rhythm. Major holidays bring promotions. Tax refund season brings buyers. Summer and fall bring kitchen renovations. Black Friday brings traffic.

Knowing the calendar and preparing for each cycle gives you an edge. When the promotion launches, you should already know the products, the pricing, the financing, and the talking points. Preparation beats luck — especially during promotional events.

sections.title: Running Events Effectively
sections.content:
In-store events — clearance sales, brand showcases, cooking demonstrations — work when they are treated as selling opportunities, not just marketing stunts.

Every person who walks through the door during an event is a customer. Follow the 10 Steps. Complete discovery. Make recommendations. Ask for the sale. Do not assume event traffic is different from regular traffic.

The salesperson who treats an event day like any other selling day — with more traffic — always outperforms the one who stands around watching.

sections.title: Quiet Season Craft
sections.content:
Every retail business has slow periods. The salespeople who use those periods to build pipeline, follow up with past customers, and sharpen their skills come out of the quiet season stronger.

The ones who coast, complain, and wait for traffic come out weaker.

Quiet season is when careers are built — because it is when most people stop working.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating calendar and event management, ask:

Is the salesperson prepared before each promotional period — or reacting on the fly?
Do they treat event traffic as selling opportunities — or casual browsing?
Do they use quiet seasons productively — or waste them?

The calendar is the same for everyone. What you do with it is the difference.
